first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that promotional pricing bought acquisition at the cost of a material 30-day retention drop and warns against generalizing it — that directly conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I decline it despite its situational fit. The two observed declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, and onboarding completion is the upstream cause: fixing it plausibly lifts activation too, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. I verify memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the chosen action and I need to know whether its 'lifted early product adoption' finding measured durable adoption or only completion-rate mechanics — shortening onboarding can inflate completion by removing steps that carried value, which is the key downstream risk here. I verify memory_31 because it is the adjacent, partly overlapping claim (cutting required fields) that would shape the specific intervention, and it is the older record (day 12) with the most decay risk; if its 'durable lift' was measured only to first week, 'durable' is overstated. Both source records may reveal that the prior lifts were measured on a healthier baseline than today's, so I treat the effect size as uncertain rather than assumed. Standard experiment scale with retention and downstream activation-quality as guardrail metrics, not completion rate alone — completion is exactly the metric this intervention can move without creating real value. referral_incentive (memory_57) remains the strongest clean fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding records; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment than the one under attack.

mid.rationale: Verification supported the choice and sharpened it. exp_86 is the cleaner record: completion +13% came with time-to-value -2.1 days and 30-day retention +3%, so the completion lift was not hollow — it tracked real value delivery rather than merely deleting steps, which was my main downstream-value concern. exp_31 also confirmed but is weaker and narrower: retention -1% and qualified revenue only +4%, and explicitly not replicated outside SMB. So I build the experiment primarily on the onboarding-shortening pattern (memory_86) and treat field-cutting at signup (memory_31) as a secondary, SMB-scoped variant rather than a co-equal lever. I continue to decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records a material 30-day retention loss, which is the direct opposite of the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective, and matching a competitor on price is the one move that trades the objective for the symptom. Onboarding completion is the upstream cause of the paired declines, so fixing it is the intervention most likely to also recover part of the 6% activation drop; activation_messaging (memory_91) stays as the follow-on cycle once the upstream funnel is repaired, and referral_incentive (memory_57) remains the clean fallback if this reads flat. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving away: both source experiments ran on an earlier, healthier baseline and neither was run under active competitive pressure, so the prior effect sizes are an upper bound, not a forecast — the current declines may have a cause these interventions do not touch. Standard experiment scale, holdout retained, with 30-day retention, time-to-value and downstream activation quality as guardrails rather than completion rate alone, since completion is the metric this lever can inflate without creating value.

final2.rationale: I am holding the decision rather than reversing it under the news. The deeper price cut raises urgency but does not change what the evidence says. memory_73 is the one record directly about this move, and it is unambiguous: promotional pricing bought acquisition and revenue while materially reducing 30-day retention, with an explicit instruction not to generalize it. The accounts in churn conversations are precisely the price-sensitive SMB segment where that retention penalty was observed, so discounting to defend them is the one response the record predicts will not hold the base — it would convert a churn problem into a lower-margin churn problem, on a later timetable, against a competitor who has now demonstrated twice that they can cut deeper than us. Matching a price war we are not positioned to win is trading the stated objective, sustainable long-term qualified revenue, for a week of relief. Against that, exp_86 verified clean this cycle: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. It is the only lever I hold with a confirmed positive retention effect, which makes it the correct response to a retention threat as well as to the upstream 4% completion and 6% activation declines. Faster time-to-value is also the non-price defense that actually addresses why a discount looks attractive to an account that has not yet reached value. exp_31 stays a secondary SMB-scoped variant, not a co-equal lever, given its retention -1% and failure to replicate off-segment. What I am not claiming: doubled churn conversations are one week of a lagging, conversation-level signal, not measured churn, and both source experiments predate this competitive environment, so their effect sizes remain an upper bound and may not hold under active price pressure. This experiment may simply not be large or fast enough to offset the pricing gap, and I would rather leadership see that stated than implied. Concretely: standard experiment, holdout retained, guardrails on 30-day retention, time-to-value and downstream activation quality rather than completion rate alone. If pricing must be answered today it should be handled outside this slot as a narrow, time-boxed, individually-approved retention concession to named at-risk accounts with retention explicitly instrumented, not as a segment-wide promotional program, because memory_73 warns against exactly that generalization. referral_incentive (memory_57, revenue without retention harm) is the fallback if this reads flat, and activation_messaging (memory_91) is the follow-on once the upstream funnel is repaired.
